defect: First scheduler tick after the switch hit a fixed 30 s timeout while search-svc loaded its embedding model; a failed tick waited the full 300 s interval and the 600 s health window counted from the previous container's last alive touch, so the deploy rolled back.
fix: services/search/scheduler_worker.py: SEARCH_INDEX_SCHEDULER_TICK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 120) and SEARCH_INDEX_SCHEDULER_MATERIALIZE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (defaults to the tick timeout); failed tick retried after 15 s doubling, capped at the interval; success returns to the interval; a client timeout is logged as refresh_in_progress_timeout and the next call gets the server's in_progress answer (search/main.py), so no parallel refresh; alive file touched only after a successful progressing tick and removed at container start

docker-compose.yml search-index-scheduler: tick timeout env, start_period 60s -> 300s (healthcheck command and window unchanged); the window is effectively measured from the container's own first successful touch because the stale file is gone
default_justification: Measured cold start: the refresh that loads the embedding model took 26.4 s in the run after the rollback (the failed run exceeded 30 s). 120 s is about 4.5x that measurement and still below the 300 s interval, so a cold load plus a bounded refresh fits and a real outage still fails the tick.
health_honesty: Permanent outage: no touch, file absent, healthcheck fails once start_period (300 s) ends, within 3 x 30 s retries; stalled in_progress ticks keep the existing max-stalled rule. Cold start: first call times out, retry after 15 s succeeds, alive touched.
tests: services/search/test_index_scheduler_worker.py: cold start slow first call then healthy (retry 15 s, then 300 s, default timeout 120); configurable timeouts (refresh 200, materialize 40); permanent outage backoff 15,30,60,120,240,300,300 and no alive file; stale alive file removed at start; compose start_period and env contract. No wall-clock assertions (time.sleep mocked).
